title: A Year from Now
theme: living in the end, the long view

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Hello, and welcome back to Imagination Nights. [pause 3]

Settle into the bed. Pull the covers up to where you like them. [pause 8]

Take one deep breath, and let it go with a sigh. [pause 8]

Now let your breathing find its own pace. You do not have to control it. Just notice it. [pause 10]

Feel your feet getting heavy. Your legs. Your back sinking into the mattress. [pause 10]

Now let us relax the body, one part at a time. You do not have to do anything. Just notice each part as I name it, and let it get heavy. [pause 8]

Your feet. Let them be warm and heavy. [pause 15]

Your calves and your knees. Heavy. [pause 15]

Your hips and your lower back. Let them sink. [pause 15]

Your belly. Let it rise and fall on its own. [pause 15]

Your chest. Your shoulders. Your arms, all the way down to your fingertips. [pause 15]

Your neck. Your face. The little muscles around your eyes. [pause 15]

Your whole body, heavy and warm, held by the bed. [pause 15]

The day is finished. This part of the night is yours. [pause 8]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Tonight we finish this set with a longer view. A year from now. [pause 13]

Picture yourself a year from tonight, lying in bed, thinking back over the year. The wishes you carried this year have had time to grow. Some of them are part of your ordinary life now. [pause 15]

In this practice you look back, not forward. You remember the year as if it has already happened. You notice how you changed. How you got through the hard parts. What surprised you. [pause 15]

Looking back from the end is the heart of living in the end. It lets your mind rest in the finished picture instead of the unfinished road. [pause 15]

You do not have to fill in every month. Let your mind skip around, the way memory does. A smell, a face, a moment of laughter. Whatever comes up is enough. [pause 5]

As always, this is imagination and feeling, not a promise. Real life will have its own turns. But tonight you can fall asleep looking back on a good year. [pause 20]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
It is a year from tonight. You are lying in bed, much like now. [pause 28]

Notice the room. Is it the same room, or a different one? [pause 31]

Let your mind drift back over the year. Start with the spring. What happened? [pause 31]

Then the summer. A day you remember. A meal. A trip. A conversation. [pause 31]

Then the fall. Something you finished. Something you let go. [pause 31]

Then the winter. A quiet night, much like this one. [pause 34]

Now think of the wish you have carried this year. Picture it as part of your life now. Ordinary. Familiar. [pause 34]

Notice how you feel about the person you were a year ago. Be kind to them. They were doing their best. [pause 34]

Say in your mind, it was a good year. I am glad I kept going. [pause 36]

Let the whole year rest in your chest, like a long breath out. [pause 36]

And let the year from now and this night become one quiet night. [pause 36]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
We will end here for tonight. [pause 10]

Keep the feeling, not the effort. Let the effort go. [pause 15]

Whatever happens tomorrow, tonight you practiced feeling at peace. That is worth something on its own. [pause 20]

Let sleep come when it comes. There is no rush. [pause 20]

Notice the weight of the covers. The cool side of the pillow. The dark. [pause 25]

Let each breath out be a little longer than the one before. [pause 25]

Nothing more to picture. Nothing more to try. Only rest. [pause 30]

Good night. [pause 60]
